system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In June 2025, did the Thai Labour Protection Act as then in force give employees the right to leave to assist a spouse who had given birth? Answer briefly.
raw_response:
**Short answer: No.**

As of June 2025, the Thai **Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998)**, as amended (the most recent substantive amendment being the Labour Protection Act (No. 7) B.E. 2562 (2019)), did **not** contain any provision granting private-sector employees a right to paid or unpaid leave specifically to assist a spouse who has given birth (i.e., no "paternity leave" or spousal-support leave).

The Act's leave provisions cover matters such as sick leave (Section 32), personal leave/business leave ("kit-jampen") of at least 3 days per year (Section 34), annual leave (Section 30), and maternity leave for female employees of up to 98 days (Section 41), but there is no corresponding entitlement for a male employee (or non-birthing spouse) to take leave to care for a spouse who has just given birth.

The 15-day "paternity leave" that is sometimes referenced in Thai public discourse applies only to **male civil servants (government officials)** under the civil service regulations (Cabinet resolutions and Office of the Civil Service Commission regulations), not to employees in the private sector governed by the Labour Protection Act. Private-sector employers may grant such leave voluntarily or through internal work rules/collective agreements, but this is not a statutory right under the Labour Protection Act itself.
